entries.topic: Decision-makers in Israel and in Hamas

claims.text: Ben-Gvir said in January 2025: 'If this irresponsible agreement is approved and implemented, the Jewish Power Party will not be part of the government and will leave it', and that aid and utilities must be 'completely stopped' to force the captives' release; he called on Smotrich to quit too.

Smotrich told his party in January 2025 he was developing an 'operational plan' to move Gazans out of the territory, long advocating what he calls 'voluntary emigration', and threatened to leave the government if such policies were not implemented after the ceasefire's first phase.

Haniyeh was killed in Tehran in July 2024 (Israel confirmed in December); Yahya Sinwar was killed by the Israeli military in Gaza in October 2024; Israel said Deif was killed in a July 2024 strike in Khan Younis, Marwan Issa in March 2024 and Mohammad Sinwar in May 2025; Khalil al-Hayya, based in Qatar, is seen as Hamas's most influential figure abroad and sits on a five-man leadership council.
Ben-Gvir resigned on 21 January 2025; Otzma Yehudit rejoined the government on 18 March 2025, hours after the truce collapsed.

On 17 February 2025 Netanyahu said he was 'committed to US President Trump's plan for the creation of a different Gaza'; Defence Minister Israel Katz announced a body to oversee 'voluntary departure' from Gaza.

On 21 May 2025 Netanyahu called the Trump plan 'so revolutionary', summarized 'Residents of Gaza who want to leave can leave', and listed its implementation among five conditions for ending the war, with the hostages' release, Hamas's surrender, its leaders' expulsion and demilitarization.

entries.topic: The United States and the mediators

claims.text: Between October 2023 and November 2024 the UN Security Council held 14 votes on Gaza; four resolutions passed (15 Nov 2023, 22 Dec 2023, 25 Mar 2024, 10 Jun 2024, the last a US draft); the US vetoed drafts on 18 Oct 2023, 25 Oct 2023, 8 Dec 2023, 20 Feb 2024, 18 Apr 2024 (Palestinian UN membership) and 20 Nov 2024; Russia and China vetoed US drafts on 25 Oct 2023 and 22 Mar 2024.

In September 2025 the US cast the only vote against a Security Council Gaza ceasefire draft, its sixth such veto; deputy envoy Morgan Ortagus said it did not condemn Hamas or recognize Israel's right to self-defence and 'seeks to return to a failed system'.

On 4 February 2025 Trump said 'The U.S. will take over the Gaza Strip ... We'll own it', spoke of 'the Riviera of the Middle East' and proposed Gazans relocate to other countries; Hamas called the statements irresponsible; Abbas rejected it; Saudi Arabia rejected displacement.

The 20-point plan (29–30 Sep 2025): a Board of Peace chaired by Trump including Tony Blair; a temporary apolitical Palestinian committee; tunnels and weapons dismantled under independent monitoring; amnesty for Hamas members who surrender weapons; Israeli troops to pull back in phases as an International Stabilisation Force takes control; 'No resident will be forced to leave'; governance until PA reforms; 'conditions may finally exist for Palestinian self-determination and statehood'.
The October 2025 truce was mediated by the US, Qatar, Turkey and Egypt.

On 4 June 2025 the US was the only vote against a Gaza ceasefire draft (14 in favour); acting ambassador Dorothy Shea said it did not condemn Hamas or urge it to disarm and 'draws false equivalence' between Israel and Hamas.

On 3 October 2025 Hamas announced 'approval of releasing all occupation prisoners — both living and remains' and readiness 'to hand over the administration of the Gaza Strip to a Palestinian body of independents (technocrats)', and to negotiate details through mediators; it did not say whether it would disarm.
